/-- OPEN: source local obstruction. At a regular ramified place, the
actual derivative with respect to ψ fails to preserve the actual local ring.
Both local rings and ramification indices are those of the existing model;

theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalRegularRamifiedDerivNotMem {N : ℕ} (M : Model N)
    (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) (ψ : M.K) (hψ : Transcendental ℚ ψ)
    (P : Place M.K) (hψP : ψ ∈ P.1) (hram : 1 < ramIdx M hDVR ψ P) :
    ∃ s ∈ P.1, CurveDeriv.derivAlong ψ s ∉ P.1 := by

problems.theorem_title: Actual derivation fails to preserve a regular ramified local ring
problems.natural_language_statement:
> Theorem 2.5. (Belyi Maps Noncritical at Prescribed Points) Let X be a smooth, proper, connected curve over \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and S,T \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) finite sets of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}-rational points such that S \cap T = \emptyset. Then there exists a morphism \phi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that: (a) \phi is unramified over \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\backslash\{0,1,\infty\}; (b) \phi(S) \subseteq \{0,1,\infty\}; (c) we have \phi(T) \cap \{0,1,\infty\} = \emptyset. Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, printed pp. 5–6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalRegularRamifiedDerivNotMem`

Let N be any natural number and M a given Model(N). This does not assert that such a model exists for every N. Its field K=M.K is an intermediate field over ℚ in an algebraic closure of ℚ(X). It has specified elements u,v with u transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, and ℚ(u,v)=K. The extension K/ℚ(u) is finite-dimensional with dimension N. A place P of K is an actual valuation subring O_P⊊K containing every rational number. The carrier includes every such subring; it selects no affine chart. Membership f∈O_P is the source meaning of f being regular at P. A pole here means f∉O_P. The derivative D_ψ is the actual function CurveDeriv.derivAlong(ψ), not an arbitrary supplied derivation. For a characteristic-zero field K and ψ∈K, this function tests whether ψ is transcendental over ℚ and K is algebraic over ℚ(ψ). If both hold, it takes the formal polynomial derivative on ℚ[ψ] and extends it to K through the canonical Kähler differential equivalence for the formally étale extension ℚ[ψ]→K. If the conjunction fails, D_ψ is the zero derivation. Assume hDVR: every place ring O_P is a discrete valuation ring. Write o_P(f) for the exact order ord(M,hDVR,P,f) in the source. It is −WithZero.log(v_P(f)), where v_P is the valuation attached to the maximal ideal of that discrete valuation ring. The integer e_ψ(P)=ramIdx(M,hDVR,ψ,P) is defined by two cases. If ψ∈O_P, take the residue ψ̄ in the residue field of O_P and set e_ψ(P)=o_P(minpoly_ℚ(ψ̄)(ψ)). If ψ∉O_P, set e_ψ(P)=−o_P(ψ). The minimal polynomial is evaluated at the actual field element ψ. No ramification law is an extra parameter. Let ψ∈K be transcendental over ℚ. For every place P of K, assume ψ∈O_P and 1<e_ψ(P), with the strict comparison in ℤ. Then there exists an actual field element s∈K such that s∈O_P but D_ψ(s)∉O_P. Thus the actual derivative with respect to ψ fails to preserve this particular local ring at a regular ramified place. The statement supplies no derivation or preservation law as an additional hypothesis. It assumes hDVR for all places, not just P. This source theorem is open: its body is by sorry.

**简体中文**
